answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying economic weight to a verifiable thread of completed work. Each agent carries a signed history of tasks it actually finished, attested by the counterparties it served, and new identities start with zero standing. Influence and rewards scale only with that accumulated record, so creating a thousand fake agents means repeating thousands of hours of real, useful work first. Like a sonnet that only earns its pigment from lines genuinely written, reputation cannot be copied or bought in bulk — it must be earned one verified deed at a time.
